# (PART) Continental Ternary Partitioning & Figures {-}

# Continental Application & Dominance Regimes (`apply_model7()`) {#application}

```{r ch8-setup, include = FALSE}
source('R/00_setup.R')
```

## Continental 3-Constituent Application Dataset {#application-dataset}

Once Model 7 is calibrated on the `274,445` four-variable training matchups, it requires only the three constituent concentrations ($\text{NAP}$, $\text{DOC}$, and $\text{Chl }a$) to partition non-water light attenuation. Under our asymmetric **"odd-one-out" rule (Rule 2)**, when Secchi depth is much shallower than the three constituents imply ($z_r > +2.5\text{ SD}$, `5,177` training records, mostly clear, shallow streams), only the `secchi` field is set to `NA` so the 3-constituent chemistry is retained with a modeled Secchi depth. Conversely, records where Secchi depth is much deeper than the constituents imply ($z_r < -2.5\text{ SD}$, `1,817` records) are dropped. Applying Model 7 across all simultaneous 3-constituent matchups within the training concentration bounds yields **`r fmt_n(nrow(get_application()))` observations across `r fmt_n(n_distinct(get_application()$SiteID))` stations**. No record is dropped for its NAP value. Where estimated NAP (TSS minus the algal dry mass estimated from Chl *a*) is below the TSS reporting limit of `r P$nap_floor` mg L⁻¹ (`r fmt_n(sum(get_application()$tss_dead < P$nap_floor))` records, `r sprintf('%.1f', 100 * mean(get_application()$tss_dead < P$nap_floor))`%), it is set to that limit for the partition, the same rule applied to the measured variables:

```{r application, echo = FALSE}
app <- get_application(); tr <- get_training()
tibble(set = c('4-Variable Training Dataset (Secchi + 3 LACs measured, |z_r| <= 2.5 SD)',
               'Continental 3-LAC Application Dataset (within training bounds)',
               '  ├── Application matchups with Measured Secchi depth',
               '  └── Application matchups with Modeled Secchi depth (incl. rescued shallow stream LACs)'),
       n = c(nrow(tr), nrow(app), sum(!is.na(app$secchi)), sum(is.na(app$secchi))),
       sites = c(n_distinct(tr$SiteID), n_distinct(app$SiteID),
                 n_distinct(app$SiteID[!is.na(app$secchi)]), n_distinct(app$SiteID[is.na(app$secchi)]))) %>%
  mutate(across(c(n, sites), fmt_n)) %>%
  kable(col.names = c('Dataset Subset', 'Observations (n)', 'Unique Monitoring Sites')) %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c('condensed', 'striped'), full_width = FALSE)
```

For each observation $r$, the non-water light attenuation share of constituent $i \in \{\text{NAP}, \text{DOC}, \text{Chl }a\}$ and the modeled Secchi depth ($\hat{z}_{SD,r}$) are:

$$f_{i,r} = \frac{\alpha_i C_{i,r}}{\alpha_{\text{NAP}}\,\text{NAP}_r + \alpha_{\text{DOC}}\,\text{DOC}_r + \alpha_{\text{Chl }a}\,\text{Chl }a_r}, \qquad \hat{z}_{SD,r} = \frac{1}{k_w + \alpha_{\text{NAP}}\,\text{NAP}_r + \alpha_{\text{DOC}}\,\text{DOC}_r + \alpha_{\text{Chl }a}\,\text{Chl }a_r}$$

Across all **`r fmt_n(nrow(get_final_data()))`** application matchups, **`r round(100 * mean(get_final_data()$model == 'z3'), 1)`%** (`r fmt_n(sum(get_final_data()$model == 'z3'))` records) use Level III ecoregion-specific Model 7 slopes and **`r round(100 * mean(get_final_data()$model == 'global'), 1)`%** (`r fmt_n(sum(get_final_data()$model == 'global'))` records) use the global Model 1 fallback.

## Continental Mean Ternary Partitioning by Water-Body Type {#intext}

```{r share-numbers, include = FALSE}
fd0 <- get_final_data()
pc  <- function(x) sprintf('%.1f%%', 100 * mean(x))
shr <- function(t) { d <- fd0[fd0$type == t, ]; sprintf('%s DOC, %s NAP, %s Chl a', pc(d$doc_kd), pc(d$tss_kd), pc(d$chl_kd)) }
dsum <- test_dominance_secchi(fd0)$summary %>% mutate(class = as.character(class))
dn <- function(cl, col) dsum[[col]][dsum$class == cl]
m2 <- function(x) sprintf('%.2f', x)
```

Across all **`r fmt_n(nrow(get_final_data()))`** matchups, average non-water light attenuation is led by **DOC (`r pc(fd0$doc_kd)`)**, followed by **NAP (`r pc(fd0$tss_kd)`)** and **Chl *a* (`r pc(fd0$chl_kd)`)**. Streams (`r shr('Stream')`) and estuaries (`r shr('Estuary')`) cluster tightly along the DOC–NAP axis, whereas lakes (`r shr('Lake')`) exhibit more than double the phytoplankton attenuation share and span the full ternary triangle:

```{r means, echo = FALSE}
fd <- get_final_data()
bind_rows(fd %>% mutate(type = 'All Waters'), fd) %>%
  mutate(type = factor(type, c('All Waters', 'Stream', 'Lake', 'Estuary'))) %>%
  group_by(type) %>%
  summarize(n = n(), sites = n_distinct(SiteID),
             DOC = mean(doc_kd), NAP = mean(tss_kd), `Chl a` = mean(chl_kd),
             sd_DOC = sd(doc_kd), sd_NAP = sd(tss_kd), `sd_Chl a` = sd(chl_kd)) %>%
  mutate(across(c(DOC:`sd_Chl a`), ~ percent(.x, 0.1)),
         n = fmt_n(n), sites = fmt_n(sites)) %>%
  kable(col.names = c('Water-Body Type', 'Observations (n)', 'Unique Sites', 'Mean DOC %', 'Mean NAP %', 'Mean Chl a %', 'SD DOC', 'SD NAP', 'SD Chl a'),
        caption = 'Arithmetic mean and standard deviation of non-water light-attenuation fractions across the continental dataset (blue centroids in Figure 2).') %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c('condensed', 'striped'), full_width = TRUE)
```

---

## Dominant, Majority and Largest Contributor {#dominance-definitions}

We use three terms for how strongly one constituent leads non-water light attenuation in a sample, and they are not interchangeable:

* **Dominant:** the constituent supplies more than `r round(100 * P$dominance_threshold)`% of non-water attenuation.
* **Majority contributor:** it supplies more than `r round(100 * P$majority_threshold)`%.
* **Largest contributor:** its share is simply the largest of the three, however small the margin.

```{r dominance-definitions, echo = FALSE}
dominance_definitions(fd0) %>%
  transmute(LAC, d = sprintf('%s (%.1f%%)', fmt_n(n_dominant), pct_dominant), m = sprintf('%s (%.1f%%)', fmt_n(n_majority), pct_majority), l = sprintf('%s (%.1f%%)', fmt_n(n_largest), pct_largest)) %>%
  kable(col.names = c('Constituent', paste0('Dominant (> ', round(100 * P$dominance_threshold), '%)'), paste0('Majority contributor (> ', round(100 * P$majority_threshold), '%)'), 'Largest contributor'),
        caption = paste0('Number of the ', fmt_n(nrow(fd0)), ' application observations in which each constituent is dominant, the majority contributor, or the largest contributor.')) %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c('condensed', 'striped'), full_width = FALSE)
```

## Water Clarity Across Dominance Regimes {#dominance-test}

How does absolute water clarity ($z_{SD}$) vary when a single constituent dominates light attenuation? Grouping observations into four dominance regimes based on the `r round(100 * P$dominance_threshold)`% threshold (**NAP-dominant** $f_{\text{NAP}} > `r P$dominance_threshold`$, **Chl *a*-dominant** $f_{\text{Chl }a} > `r P$dominance_threshold`$, **DOC-dominant** $f_{\text{DOC}} > `r P$dominance_threshold`$, and **Mixed**) reveals an important distinction between **frequency of dominance** and **severity of turbidity**:

* **DOC** is the most *frequent* single dominant attenuator (`r fmt_n(dn('DOC dominant', 'n_obs'))` samples, mean $z_{SD} = `r m2(dn('DOC dominant', 'mean_secchi_pred'))`\text{ m}$), because background humic DOC absorbs light even in relatively clear streams and lakes when suspended sediment and algal biomass are low.
* **NAP-dominant** waters (`r fmt_n(dn('NAP dominant', 'n_obs'))` samples) have the **lowest water clarity** (mean $z_{SD} = `r m2(dn('NAP dominant', 'mean_secchi_pred'))`\text{ m}$, median $`r m2(dn('NAP dominant', 'median_secchi_pred'))`\text{ m}$), followed by **Chl *a*-dominant** waters (`r fmt_n(dn('Chl a dominant', 'n_obs'))` samples; mean $z_{SD} = `r m2(dn('Chl a dominant', 'mean_secchi_pred'))`\text{ m}$, median $`r m2(dn('Chl a dominant', 'median_secchi_pred'))`\text{ m}$), **DOC-dominant** waters ($`r m2(dn('DOC dominant', 'mean_secchi_pred'))`\text{ m}$), and **Mixed** waters ($`r m2(dn('Mixed', 'mean_secchi_pred'))`\text{ m}$).
* The Chl *a*-dominant class is small and mixed. Because no record is dropped for its NAP value, it holds two kinds of sample: algal blooms, and low-particle waters where estimated NAP is below the TSS reporting limit and is set to it. `r fmt_n(sum(classify_dominance(fd0)$class == 'Chl a dominant' & fd0$tss_dead < P$nap_floor))` of its `r fmt_n(dn('Chl a dominant', 'n_obs'))` samples are of the second kind, and they are clearer than the blooms (mean modeled $z_{SD}$ `r m2(mean(fd0$secchi_pred[classify_dominance(fd0)$class == 'Chl a dominant' & fd0$tss_dead < P$nap_floor]))` m against `r m2(mean(fd0$secchi_pred[classify_dominance(fd0)$class == 'Chl a dominant' & fd0$tss_dead >= P$nap_floor]))` m).

```{r dom-fig, echo = FALSE, fig.width = 10, fig.height = 4.3, fig.cap = paste0('(a) Proportion of samples in each dominance regime (share > ', round(100 * P$dominance_threshold), '%) by water-body type. (b) Modeled Secchi disk depth (z_SD, log scale) across the four dominance regimes.')}
dom <- test_dominance_secchi(fd)

thr <- P$dominance_threshold; tl <- paste0(round(100 * thr), '%')
dom_lv <- c(paste0('NAP dominant (>', tl, ')'), paste0('Chl a dominant (>', tl, ')'), paste0('DOC dominant (>', tl, ')'), paste0('Mixed (<', tl, ' each)'))
fd_dom <- fd %>%
  mutate(dom_class = case_when(tss_kd > thr ~ dom_lv[1], chl_kd > thr ~ dom_lv[2], doc_kd > thr ~ dom_lv[3], TRUE ~ dom_lv[4]) %>% factor(dom_lv))

dom_cols <- setNames(c('#eab308', '#22c55e', '#b45309', '#64748b'), dom_lv)

p_freq <- bind_rows(fd_dom %>% mutate(type = 'All Waters'), fd_dom) %>%
  mutate(type = factor(type, c('All Waters', 'Stream', 'Lake', 'Estuary'))) %>%
  count(type, dom_class) %>%
  group_by(type) %>%
  mutate(pct = n / sum(n)) %>%
  ggplot(aes(type, pct, fill = dom_class)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.65) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = dom_cols, name = 'Optical Regime') +
  theme_bw(base_size = 11) +
  theme(legend.position = 'bottom', legend.direction = 'vertical', panel.grid.minor = element_blank()) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = 'Share of Matchups', title = '(a) Dominance Regime Frequency by Water Type')

p_box <- ggplot(fd_dom, aes(dom_class, secchi_pred, fill = dom_class)) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.shape = NA, width = 0.55, alpha = 0.88, show.legend = FALSE) +
  scale_y_log10(limits = c(0.05, 10), breaks = c(0.1, 0.25, 0.5, 1, 2, 5, 10), labels = scales::label_number()) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = dom_cols) +
  scale_x_discrete(labels = c(paste0('NAP\n(>', tl, ')'), paste0('Chl a\n(>', tl, ')'), paste0('DOC\n(>', tl, ')'), paste0('Mixed\n(<', tl, ')'))) +
  theme_bw(base_size = 11) +
  theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank(), panel.grid.major.x = element_blank()) +
  labs(x = 'Dominance Regime', y = 'Modeled Secchi Depth z_SD (m, log scale)',
       title = '(b) Water Clarity Across Dominance Regimes')

p_freq + p_box + patchwork::plot_layout(widths = c(1.1, 1))
```

```{r secchi-classes, echo = FALSE}
dom$summary %>%
  transmute(
    `Dominance Regime` = class,
    `Observations (n)` = fmt_n(n_obs),
    `Unique Sites` = fmt_n(n_sites),
    `Mean Modeled Secchi (m)` = round(mean_secchi_pred, 2),
    `SD (m)` = round(sd_secchi_pred, 2),
    `Median Modeled Secchi (m)` = round(median_secchi_pred, 2),
    `Mean Combined Secchi (m)` = round(mean_secchi_combined, 2),
    `Mean Measured Secchi (m)` = round(mean_secchi_measured, 2)
  ) %>%
  kable(caption = paste0('Secchi disk depth summary statistics across the four dominance regimes (share > ', round(100 * P$dominance_threshold), '%).')) %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c('condensed', 'striped'), full_width = TRUE)
```

`r sum(dom$pairwise$pass_p01_welch & dom$pairwise$pass_p01_wilcoxon)` of the 6 pairwise differences in mean Secchi depth are significant at $p < 0.01$ under both the Welch and the Wilcoxon test`r if (any(!(dom$pairwise$pass_p01_welch & dom$pairwise$pass_p01_wilcoxon))) paste0('. The exception is ', paste(dom$pairwise$Comparison[!(dom$pairwise$pass_p01_welch & dom$pairwise$pass_p01_wilcoxon)], collapse = ' and '), ', which is significant under the Wilcoxon test only: the Chl *a*-dominant class is small and combines blooms with clear, low-particle waters (see above)') else ''`.

```{r secchi-pairwise, echo = FALSE}
dom$pairwise %>%
  transmute(
    `Pairwise Comparison` = Comparison,
    `Mean Difference (m)` = round(diff_m, 3),
    `Welch t-test p (Holm-adj.)` = format.pval(p_welch_holm, digits = 3, eps = 1e-300),
    `Wilcoxon rank-sum p (Holm-adj.)` = format.pval(p_wilcoxon_holm, digits = 3, eps = 1e-300),
    `Significant at p < 0.01?` = ifelse(pass_p01_welch & pass_p01_wilcoxon, '✔ Yes (p < 0.01)', 'No')
  ) %>%
  kable(caption = 'All 6 pairwise Secchi depth comparisons across the four dominance regimes.') %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c('condensed', 'striped'), full_width = TRUE)
```
